parsed.doc_summary: News article on Santa Ana's ordinance banning algorithmic rent-setting software (first reading Feb. 17, 2026; final vote set for March 3, 2026). Describes prohibition, exemptions, and tenant civil enforcement up to $1,000 per violation.

rules.title: Santa Ana ban on algorithmic rent-setting software
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use, and vendors may not sell, license or provide, algorithmic rent-setting software that uses nonpublic competitor data for residential rentals in Santa Ana. Tenants can sue for injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation plus attorney's fees.
rules.quoted_span: prohibits the sale, licensing, provision and use of certain algorithmic rent-setting software for residential rental properties.
rules.effective_date_note: Article states only first reading on Feb. 17, 2026 and final vote set for March 3, 2026; effective date not stated and adoption not confirmed in the article. Ordinance number is not in the document, so it is taken from the task context.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data; civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation
rules.penalty: Injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, plus attorney's fees
rules.exemptions: Pricing software relying solely on publicly available data, aggregate historical data, or tools used to comply with affordable housing program requirements
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property within Santa Ana city limits
rules.interaction: Operates alongside existing and proposed state antitrust laws while providing stronger local protections
rules.conflict_note: Document describes the ordinance at first reading with a final vote pending (March 3, 2026), so adoption and effective date are unconfirmed here.

unverifiable_exemptions: software relying solely on public data, aggregate historical data, or affordable housing compliance tools
